result.summary:
Fourth run of R6, picking up where the previous run stopped (STAND.md, same worktree, head bb38876 = origin). The code has been frozen since bb38876. This run regenerated the Modern change detectors (3 of 6 pictures changed on purpose, each compared against the base picture, commit c8b18d1, pushed), ran every gate, recorded the three missing clips, ran the head-vs-base performance comparison and finished bericht.md.

Result on c8b18d1 (all measured, llvmpipe, load 15–26):
- Import is clean and check_scripts reports 316 scripts with 0 errors.
- Arcade is picture-identical: 20 of 20 and 17 of 17.
- Modern change detectors: 6 of 6 identical, and the OpenGL ES comparison is OK.
- modern_sight --full and modern_path_check --full are OK.
- run_render_checks all: 21 of 21 files OK, including structures, start_km0, light_base and terrain_cover with K1.
- run_tests: 759 tests with 3 failures. All three are real-time audio tests ("in the running game"), and on the unchanged base copy the same tests fail under the same load, so they are not caused by R6.
- Full Modern autopilot run on DEV at 21:00: no script errors. render() is about 0.4 ms slower on average; commits on the main thread stay small.

There are four clips at 60 fps: countdown with LOS, refuelling at km 15 (18 L), radar flash plus police stop, and the finish banner. I watched all of them and they show the same sequence as Arcade.

Look against Arcade:
- By day: clearly better at the fuel station, the border and the city.
- At night: equal to better at the border and in the city. The fuel station at night is different but not better.
- Start/finish and the speed camera: equivalent, no visible gain.
- On DEV the border roof stands on the right without a pillar (F1/F7, contract issue).

result.look_verdict:
Compared against Arcade frames of the same simulation state:

- Fuel station by day: clearly better. Real canopies with red and white fascia bands, columns with plinths, the island with its yellow kerb, AS1b pumps and building, the price pylon, and "TANKSTELLE" in Arcade's lettering.
- Fuel station at night: different, not better. Arcade's station glows warmly as a whole because of its building sprite; Modern's AS1b building stands further right and is dimmer. The lane is 0.90 × Arcade's brightness (measured).
- Border by day: better in depth and detail (roof underside, lamps, booths as models; Prague–Nürnberg is clearly better). On DEV the roof stands on the right without any pillar and looks unsupported.
- Border at night: equal to better.
- City: better. Lamps with mast and arm, pools as bright as Arcade's, hedges and fences as solid bodies.
- Start/finish: equivalent, no visible gain. Same banner panels, steel posts instead of white beams; the finish banner now lights up at night like Arcade's.
- Speed camera: equivalent. The glow at the camera head is easier to see in the clip than in Arcade.
- All four clip sequences are identical to Arcade (same simulation).

What is missing for "clearly better": the fuel station at night, and a visible gain at start/finish.

result.verdict: Nothing in R6 (c8b18d1) is broken. The Arcade picture gates match 20 of 20 and 17 of 17. modern_sight --full and modern_path_check --full pass. The structure, start_km0, light_base and terrain_cover render checks pass, including K1. A full-test-stage Rule 3 run gives the same result and the same traffic hashes in all 400 seconds. In run_tests.sh, 759 tests ran: two real-time audio tests and the Attract 'idle' check failed, all three load-related and not caused by R6. The network scan found every station, border, gantry, radar and street light where Arcade draws it, with 0 mismatches in 5366 chunks. File ownership is clean apart from two reported foreign files, and no frozen file is touched. My main finding: 5 of 48 border roofs have no pillar at all on the right (R6 reported 4), so the roof visibly floats where Arcade draws two pillars. Second finding (F1): the extra columns at the end of each canopy hide parts of distant signs in bends more often than Arcade's own pillars do. On the look, Modern is better than Arcade by day at the station, border and city, clearly so only at the border and in the city. At night nothing is clearly better and the finish gantry is slightly worse. Start and finish show no visible gain, and the radar is only slightly better. So the 'clearly better than Arcade' goal is met only by day and for three of five elements. Nothing looks worse than the base 6e48405. render() time at normal speed shows no measurable difference from the base. No blocker for test build 2; B-01 should be decided before it ships.

findings.problem: Arcade's front pillar moves out as front_out when a sign stands under the roof. It is then dropped like any non-Arcade pillar when it stands in a bend corridor, and so is the end pillar. 5 of 48 roofs have no pillar on the right, where Arcade draws two front pillars, so the roof floats. R6 reports 4.

result.summary:
This was a fresh start, with no predecessor. I fast-forwarded to c8b18d1, reproduced every QA-R6 finding and fixed the confirmed ones. All numbers below are measured unless marked otherwise.

- **B-01, border roofs:** QA was right that 5 of 48 roofs float on one side. I tried and rejected QA's one-line fix, because the moved-out pillar would then stand in the bend corridor and hide 36–174 lines of sight to cars that Arcade's own pillar does not hide. Instead, the free side now hangs from two masts on the carried side, with stays to a steel edge beam, all above the slab. No roof floats anywhere in the network.

result.look_verdict:
Judged frame by frame against Arcade at the same simulation state:

- **Start and finish gantries:** now clearly better, by day and especially at night. There are white columns as in Arcade, a box truss with floodlights, a banner as red as Arcade's, and a lit start or finish line. QA had found no gain here, and the finish slightly worse at night.
- **Border by day:** better. From 50–200 m the roof reads clearly as cable-stayed (mast plus stays). From very close the fascia hides the stays, so the right side shows no pillar where Arcade draws one. It no longer floats without a visible reason.
- **Border at night:** equal to better. The fascia is brighter but still dimmer than Arcade's white fascia.
- **Fuel station by day:** better, essentially unchanged from R6.
- **Fuel station at night:** still only equal, not better. A warm spot in front of the shop is new, but Arcade's whole glowing building front is missing, because the AS1b shop model has no night picture.
- **Speed camera and city:** unchanged from R6. The radar is slightly better than Arcade, the city better.

Overall, "clearly better than Arcade" now holds for start/finish, the border by day and the city. It does not yet hold for the fuel station at night or for the speed camera.

findings.where: scripts/race3d/builders/station.gd end_column_hides() (skips cameras with not p.has(...)) with ChunkStreamer._restart (path from start - keep_behind_m 150 m)
findings.problem: The end-column decision of a canopy depends on where the race started. Cameras before path.first are skipped, so a late start keeps an end column that a race from km 0 drops. Inferred: fairness is not affected, because the skipped cameras lie behind the start. But the same station looks different between runs, and that affects A/B pictures, goldens and QA shots that start near a station.
findings.evidence: Measured with my probe bin/startdep.gd (headless, all 130 directions, logs/startdep.log). Starting 100/300/500 m before a canopy, canopy_columns() decides differently at 40/3/0 of 1909 canopies. Every difference is an extra 'end' or 'end_out' column, e.g. dortmund_frankfurt__dortmund km 11.31: from km 0 [front], late start [front, end_out].
findings.repro: godot --headless --path . -s m1/NACH-R6/bin/startdep.gd (in a worktree at 2b7dcc0); look for STARTDEP lines and the STARTDEP-SUMMARY.
findings.fix: Count cameras the path does not hold (positions before p.first) as hiding, which is conservative, or compute the decision on a path of its own that does not depend on the window. Only station.gd (R6) changes.

findings.where: station.gd collect() -> columns_in_chunk()/canopy_columns() line-of-sight check; contract §4.5.5 'collect: main thread: cheap extra snapshot'
findings.problem: The line-of-sight check runs on the main thread inside collect(). It is not a cheap snapshot: per-chunk spikes are in the same range as the 3 ms chunk-commit budget of the deck preset, and the contract sets no budget for collect().
findings.evidence: Measured with QA's collect_time.gd on DEV (path 36 chunks ahead, load ~12): station max 3.22 ms per chunk at km 12.48 (a canopy decided one roof ahead), average 0.14 ms; border max 0.48 ms. FIX-R6 measured 0.34/0.60 ms on the base and 3.1-6.7 ms on the head. The Deck is not measured (inferred: smaller without the other load on this machine).
findings.fix: Lead decision: set a collect() budget, or spread the check over frames or move it into prepare() for the first stations. That needs a streamer hook from R4. Re-measure with the Leistungstest on the Deck.

findings.where: scripts/race3d/builders/border.gd _mast()/edge beam (all below the fascia top at 7.6 m)
findings.problem: On the 5 hung roofs the fascia (6.0-7.6 m) hides the stays and the edge beam in the last ~40 m before the roof. The free side then shows no visible support where Arcade draws a pillar. A stay end shows as a small striped patch at the top-right end of the fascia.
findings.evidence: Looked at: deliver/NACH-R6/02_dev_grenze_tag_nah_A_M.jpg, 04_ausschnitt_dev_grenze_nah_rechts_ohne_stuetze.jpg, 08_prag_grenze_tag_unter_dach_A_M.jpg. From 50 to 600 m (01, 05, 07) the masts and stays are clearly visible.
findings.fix: Make the support readable up close while keeping everything above the slab (F7 unchanged): for example, a steel edge girder that rises above the fascia top on the free side, or a visible truss end.

findings.where: station.gd canopy_columns() fallback: end column on the island for canopies that would otherwise have no column
findings.problem: At 3 canopies in the network, the fallback end column (Arcade has none there) hides part of a gameplay-relevant board. Worst case: an 89 % covered 'curve' warning at 210 m.

findings.fix: For the fallback, choose the candidate (island end, end_out, front_out) with the smallest measured occlusion instead of always the island end. Alternatively, accept it as a lead decision and document it.
